title: HINT for Business Analysts — requirements that trace
metaDescription: Keep requirements, business rules, scenarios and traceability beside the work so assistants report gaps instead of inventing stakeholders.
h1: Your assistant drafts quickly. HINT makes every requirement trace back.
intro: HINT keeps plain-text requirements knowledge beside your BRDs and process documents. Your assistant reads the applicable stakeholders, rules, scope and open questions before it writes.

situations.before: A BRD names a stakeholder who was never interviewed.
situations.body: Unknown owners become questions for the analyst instead of plausible names in a finished-looking document.

situations.before: A requirement contradicts a business rule stated elsewhere.
situations.body: The conflict is surfaced with both pieces of context so the analyst can make the decision explicitly.

situations.before: Alternate flows are quietly merged into the happy path.
situations.body: Main, alternate and edge paths retain their own acceptance criteria and links back to the need.

example.intro: The Initech demo grounds a TPS-reporting requirement in an approved source.
example.after: It builds the requirement from SRC-1, keeps its ID available for traceability, and lists any missing stakeholder or acceptance detail as an open question.
example.compiled:
<requirement name="tps-reporting-1">
  Approved requirement grounded in SRC-1.
</requirement>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent stakeholders, systems, figures or regulations.
Resolve contradictions between a requirement and a business rule silently.
Specify anything that the declared scope excludes.
disclaimer: HINT structures the context used to draft requirements; stakeholder validation and organizational approval remain part of your analysis process.

faq.a: It can help an assistant draft one from declared requirements and sources, and an emit pack can create derivable structure.

faq.q: Does it replace Jira or Confluence?
faq.a: No. It governs what goes into those systems; your existing tools can remain the publication and workflow layer.

faq.q: Can BA and PM hintbooks coexist?
faq.a: Yes. They share a compatible common core; put the most task-specific book first when a keyword overlaps.

keywordDescriptions.requirement: States a traceable functional need with a stable identifier.
keywordDescriptions.nfr: Captures a measurable quality constraint such as performance or security.
keywordDescriptions.bizrule: Records a business rule that requirements must not contradict.
keywordDescriptions.usecase: Defines an actor, goal and trigger for an interaction.
keywordDescriptions.scenario: Keeps one main or alternate flow as ordered behavior.
keywordDescriptions.acceptance: States observable conditions that make a requirement complete.
keywordDescriptions.trace: Links a need, requirement, use case and test identifier.
keywordDescriptions.scope: Draws the boundary around what the analysis covers.
